name: Paper & pulp
card: Hard intake water, salts building up as loops close, and metals carried in with recycled fibre.
title: One adaptive platform, four points in the mill
lede: Paper mills face three water challenges: hard intake water, salts building up as loops close, and metals carried in with recycled fibre. Danu Water's adaptive electromembrane separation tackles each where it arises, adjusting in real time as water quality shifts.

items.name: LoopGuard
items.tagline: Close the loop without the build-up.
items.card: Recycles WWTP effluent back to the paper machine, without the salts, keeping chemicals effective and avoiding scaling.
items.problem: As mills reuse more water, salts build up in their process water. The result is scaling, corrosion and process chemistry that stops performing.
benefits: Lower fresh water intake and effluent volume
Less scaling and corrosion, so fewer descaling shutdowns
More stable wet-end chemistry and lower additive use
Deeper loop closure than volume-based treatment allows
items.application: Takes treated effluent from the WWTP, removes the salts that limit reuse, and returns the water to the mill. Adaptive electromembrane separation adjusts in real time as effluent quality shifts.

illus.without: Salts build up as scale and narrow the bore
illus.with: Salts removed, the bore stays clear

flow.legend: Reuse loop: treated effluent back to the mill

items.name: BrightGuard
items.tagline: Recycled fibre, without the baggage.
items.card: Removes the metals behind corrosion, deposits and chemistry problems.
items.problem: Recycled fibre brings metals into the mill. As internal loops close they accumulate, and their effects reach well beyond bleaching: into equipment, process chemistry, product quality and the effluent.
benefits: Lower corrosion and deposit risk across pipework, chests and clothing
More stable wet-end chemistry and additive performance
Less bleaching chemical wasted and lower chelant use
Fewer specks and better brightness stability
Cleaner sludge, more disposal options, easier discharge compliance
items.application: A kidney on an internal loop, such as the deinking loop: it draws off water, removes the metals and returns it. Applies across packaging and white grades.

illus.without: Metals discolour the water and drop out as deposits
illus.with: Metals removed, the water runs clear

grid.title: Where metals cause problems
items: Dissolved copper and iron accelerate corrosion of steel pipework and equipment, and feed the bacteria behind microbially induced corrosion.
Iron and manganese oxidise and drop out on wires, felts and pipework, and show up as specks and discolouration in the sheet.
Multivalent metals disrupt sizing, retention aids, dyes and optical brighteners, so additive doses creep up.
Transition metals decompose bleaching chemicals and drive brightness loss and reversion.
Metal loads can restrict sludge disposal routes and put discharge consents at risk.
Chelants mask metals rather than remove them, adding cost plus nitrogen and COD to the effluent.

items.name: MineralClear
items.tagline: Softening without the salt.
items.card: Chemical-free softening for hard intake water, giving your process the best quality starting point.
items.problem: Hard river or borehole water carries calcium, magnesium and bicarbonate alkalinity that scale boilers, heat exchangers and process lines. Conventional fixes swap one problem for another: ion-exchange brine adds chloride to the loop, lime softening makes sludge, and RO costs energy and leaves a concentrate to manage.
benefits: No regenerant chemicals and no added chloride
Hardness removal tuned to target, not over-treated
Follows seasonal swings in intake quality
Protects boilers, heat exchangers and process lines
items.application: Treats hard intake water before it enters the mill, giving the process the best possible starting point. Add TraceClear where some uses, such as certain boilers, need extra-low conductivity.

illus.without: Limescale coats tubes and cuts heat transfer
illus.with: Clean surfaces and efficient heat transfer

items.name: TraceClear
items.tagline: Extra-low conductivity, where it counts.
items.card: For cases requiring extra-low conductivity, including some boiler applications, this added step comes after MineralClear.
items.problem: Some uses, including certain boilers and high-purity applications, need water with far lower conductivity than softening alone delivers.
benefits: Extra-low conductivity for the uses that need it
Treats only the share of water that needs it
Builds on MineralClear, so the two work as a pair
items.application: An added step after MineralClear for cases that need extra-low conductivity, including some boiler applications.

name: Textiles manufacturing
card: Reuse 95%+ of dyehouse water, with salt always removed to your target and colour too where you need it.
title: Reuse 95%+ of your dyehouse water
lede: Dyeing and finishing use large volumes of water and large doses of salt, and the load changes with every recipe. Danu Water turns spent dyebath and rinse water into clean process water, treated to whatever conductivity your process needs, leaving under 5% as a small concentrated stream.

items.name: Dyehouse water reuse
items.tagline: Salt out to your target. Colour too, if you need it.
items.card: Turns spent dyebath and rinse water into clean process water, with 95%+ returned for reuse.
items.problem: Dyehouse wastewater carries a high and variable salt load from dyeing and finishing, plus colour and auxiliaries such as urea and bleach. Salt affects shade consistency and dye uptake, so the water cannot simply go back into the process.
benefits: 95%+ of water returned clean and ready to reuse
Salt always removed to the conductivity your process needs
Colour reduced alongside salt where your reuse target requires it
Bleach, urea and other auxiliaries assessed case by case
Every litre reused is a litre you don't draw in or discharge, a direct step towards zero liquid discharge
items.application: Treats spent dyebath and rinse water after a dedicated pre-treatment step, returning clean water to the dyehouse. The small residual stream can be discharged, processed further or reused, depending on what is in it and the routes open to your site.

items: of water returned clean and ready to reuse
left over as a small, concentrated stream
less fresh water in and less discharge out, supporting your target

name: Tanneries
card: Very salty effluent from hide curing and processing, and chromium to keep out of the environment.
title: Salt and water management for tanneries
lede: Hides arrive preserved in salt, and much of it ends up in tannery effluent. Combined with the chemicals used in tanning, it makes tannery wastewater some of the hardest industrial water to treat or reuse.

items.name: Desalting tannery effluent
items.tagline: Take the salt out of the hardest stream.
items.card: Removes dissolved salts from treated tannery effluent, so the water can be reused and discharge limits met.
items.problem: Soaking salted hides releases large amounts of chloride, which conventional biological treatment does not remove. High-salinity discharge is increasingly restricted.
benefits: Meets tightening limits on chloride and total dissolved solids
Water recovered for soaking and washing
A concentrated salt stream rather than a large salty discharge
items.application: Treats effluent after conventional treatment, removing salts so water can return to the beamhouse.

name: Laundrettes & laundries
card: A complete on-site system that cleans wash water for reuse, so less goes to sewer at trade-effluent rates.
title: Water reuse for laundrettes and laundries
lede: Laundries use a lot of water, much of it heated, and usually send it straight to sewer at trade-effluent rates. Danu Water supplies the whole treatment train needed to clean that water on site and send it back to the machines.

items.name: Wash water reuse
items.tagline: Wash, clean, repeat.
items.card: A complete treatment train, from filtration to Danu Water's system, that sends clean water back to the machines.
items.problem: Most laundries have no on-site treatment, so every litre goes to sewer at trade-effluent rates. Detergents, softeners and hardness build up if wash water is recycled without proper treatment, leaving residues on fabrics and scale in machines.
benefits: Lower water and trade-effluent bills
Less energy spent heating fresh water
Softer, consistent water, so less detergent and less scale
Delivered as one installed system, with no treatment plant to build
items.application: Wash water passes through solids filtration, flocculation and UV to destroy residual bleach, then Danu Water's system removes the dissolved salts so the water can go back to the machines. These stages protect the membranes and come as part of the installed system. The same full train applies to any site that currently sends its wastewater to sewer.

name: Steel
card: Cut scale and corrosion across the whole works, raise cycles of concentration, and recover metals from finishing lines.
title: Scale control and recovery across the steelworks
lede: An integrated steelworks runs many different water loops, from intake and gas scrubbers to casting, rolling and finishing. Lowering conductivity at intake, and again at key loops, cuts scale and corrosion throughout the plant. That means fewer forced outages, longer equipment life and less fresh water.

items.name: Intake conditioning
items.tagline: Start every loop with better water.
items.card: Lowers conductivity at the primary intake, so every loop downstream has less work to do.
items.problem: Dissolved salts in intake water end up concentrated in every recirculating loop on site, driving scale, corrosion and blowdown wherever they go.
benefits: Less scale and corrosion across the whole works
Higher cycles of concentration in every loop
Less fresh water drawn in
Lower risk of fouling-driven failures, both safety and financial
items.application: Conditions water at the primary intake, before it is distributed across the site.

items.name: Scrubber loop control
items.tagline: Keep gas scrubbers running clean.
items.card: Controls salt build-up in sintering, blast furnace and converter gas-scrubber loops, trimming blowdown.
items.problem: Wet gas scrubbers depend on recirculating water. As it recirculates, salts concentrate and cause scale, while contaminants such as cyanide, ammonia and metals accumulate.
benefits: Better scrubber performance
Less blowdown and make-up water
A route to targeting contaminants and metals where needed
items.application: A side-stream on the scrubber recirculation loop that removes dissolved salts and returns the water. Contaminant or metals targeting is scoped and tested for each loop.

items.name: Casting and rolling cooling water
items.tagline: Tight tolerances, held steady.
items.card: Holds conductivity down in casting and rolling cooling loops, where tolerances are tightest.
items.problem: Mould cooling in continuous casting can need conductivity below 400 µS/cm. As cooling water evaporates and recirculates, salts climb until loops must be blown down.
benefits: Steady water quality for the most sensitive cooling duties
Higher cycles of concentration
Less blowdown and make-up water
items.application: Polishes the conductivity of casting and rolling cooling loops, after the solids and oil removal already on site.

items.name: Recovery from pickling and galvanising
items.tagline: The most concentrated streams on site, put to use.
items.card: Explores recovering iron, zinc and chloride from pickling rinse and galvanising wash water.
items.problem: Pickling and galvanising produce the most concentrated salt streams in a steelworks, carrying iron, zinc, chloride and ammonium that are costly to treat and valuable to recover.
benefits: Recovered metals and salts instead of waste
Less load on wastewater treatment
Rinse water returned to the line
items.application: Treats rinse and wash water from pickling and galvanising lines to recover salts and metals. Fit is assessed for each stream.

name: Mining & mine water
card: Treat mine water for reuse, polish discharge to meet permits, design water in from day one, and keep metals in leach circuits.
title: Mine water, permits and metals recovery
lede: Mining across Europe is often held back not by geology but by water. Existing operations face permit reviews and new critical-mineral projects struggle to get permitted, both blocked at meeting discharge limits. Danu Water closes that gap, and can recover saleable by-products while it does.

items.name: Final polish for permit compliance
items.tagline: Below the limit, with a by-product to sell.
items.card: Polishes treated discharge to reduce sulphate and metals further, recovering by-products such as sodium sulphate.
items.problem: Many sites already treat their water with lime or RO and still struggle with tightening sulphate and metals limits. Arguments that further treatment is infeasible or disproportionately costly are under pressure.
benefits: Sulphate and metals reduced beyond existing treatment
Saleable by-products, such as sodium sulphate, that offset the cost
Designed against all three layers of EU water law: watercourse, mine site and processing step
items.application: An electromembrane polishing step after the existing treatment train, applicable to sulphate-dominated and acid mine drainage sites.

items.name: Designed in for new projects
items.tagline: Within permit from the first day.
items.card: Built into the water design of new lithium, rare earth and other critical-mineral projects from day one.
items.problem: New processing routes, such as acid roasting for lithium, generate concentrated salt side streams by design. Retrofitting treatment later adds cost, risk and permitting delay.
benefits: Never a discharge or contamination risk
Feasibility evidence for the permit application
Recovered secondary materials that circular economy rules reward
items.application: Part of the project's water design from the outset, treating process liquors and recovering salts such as sodium sulphate.

items.name: Mine water for reuse
items.tagline: From perpetual treatment cost to water resource.
items.card: Treats pumped mine water to a quality that can be used for agriculture or industry, rather than simply discharged.
items.problem: Large volumes of mine water are pumped and treated, at closed sites in perpetuity, and then discharged with nothing recovered. Some waters are chloride-dominated, others sulphate-dominated from pyrite oxidation, so one fixed design does not fit all.
benefits: Turns a perpetual treatment cost into a water resource
Tolerates variability between and within sites
Copes with solids and scaling minerals that foul reverse osmosis
items.application: Sits after conventional mine water treatment, removing the dissolved salts that stop mine water being reused. Below about 10,000 µS/cm treatment is straightforward; higher salinities are handled with multiple units, a bespoke high-salinity design or blending.

items.name: Salt control in bioleaching
items.tagline: Keep the metals, lose the salt.
items.card: Selectively removes sodium chloride from bioleach solutions, keeping copper and iron in the circuit.
items.problem: In bioleaching, salt builds up in the recirculating solution and has to be controlled without losing copper, or the iron the bacteria reuse.
benefits: Keeps salinity where the process needs it
Retains valuable copper and reusable iron
Reduces bleed and make-up volumes
items.application: Treats a bleed of the raffinate, removing sodium chloride and returning the solution, with its iron, to the heap. Suited to heap and tank bioleaching of low and medium-grade copper ores such as chalcopyrite.

name: Distilling
card: Close the water loop in rum distillation: reuse water, potassium fertiliser and more biogas from vinasse and cooling blowdown.
title: Closing the water loop in rum distillation
lede: For every litre of rum, a distillery produces many litres of vinasse, known as dunder in the Caribbean, and many distilleries sit where fresh water is precious. Danu Water turns vinasse and cooling blowdown into reuse water, potassium fertiliser and more biogas.

items.name: Water and potassium recovery
items.tagline: From disposal problem to fertiliser.
items.card: Recovers reuse water and a potassium fertiliser product from digested vinasse.
items.problem: Vinasse is high-strength, salty and produced in large volumes. Even after digestion it is usually discharged, and the potassium it carries is wasted.
benefits: Reuse water back into the distillery
A saleable potassium sulphate fertiliser
Much less effluent discharged
items.application: Treats digested and polished vinasse, returning water to the process and producing a potassium-rich product.

items.name: More backset to fermentation
items.tagline: Return more dunder without the salt.
items.card: Removes salts from backset so more dunder can return to fermentation, saving dilution water.
items.problem: Many distilleries already return some dunder to fermentation as backset. Salt build-up limits how much they can reuse, so fresh water is used for molasses dilution instead.
benefits: Less fresh water for molasses dilution
Less vinasse sent onwards for treatment
Steadier fermentation conditions
items.application: Desalts the backset stream before it returns to fermentation.

items.name: Sulphate control for digesters
items.tagline: Less H₂S, more biogas.
items.card: Cuts sulphate ahead of anaerobic digestion, reducing hydrogen sulphide and lifting biogas output.
items.problem: Sulphate in vinasse feeds the bacteria that produce hydrogen sulphide, which inhibits digestion, corrodes equipment and lowers biogas quality.
benefits: Less hydrogen sulphide
Protected digesters
More biogas to displace fuel oil
items.application: Removes sulphate from vinasse on its way to the digesters.

items.name: Cooling blowdown recovery
items.tagline: Send blowdown back to the tower.
items.card: Desalts cooling tower blowdown and returns it to the tower, cutting make-up water.
items.problem: Cooling towers lose water through evaporation and blowdown, and the blowdown carries the salts that would otherwise cause scale.
benefits: Less cooling tower make-up water
Less discharge
Less scale in the cooling circuit
items.application: Treats blowdown from the cooling tower and returns the water to it.

highlights.note: Exemplar figures for a large molasses distillery with anaerobic digestion, modelled on public data. Not a site assessment.

name: Municipal & utilities
card: Turn treated municipal effluent into cooling water, and help data centres use harder local water instead of drinking water.
title: Effluent reuse for utilities and cooling
lede: Cooling is one of the largest uses of water in industry, and demand from data centres is rising fast. Much of it is still met with drinking-quality water. Treated municipal effluent is a reliable alternative, once the salts are dealt with.

items.name: Municipal effluent to cooling water
items.tagline: Keep drinking water for drinking.
items.card: Turns pretreated municipal effluent into cooling water, recovering minerals and making acid and base the plant can use.
items.problem: Every cubic metre of drinking water used for cooling is unavailable for homes and new development. Treated effluent is a steady local supply, but dissolved salts and hardness stop it being used for cooling.
benefits: Frees potable supply for homes and growth
Recovered salt turned into the acid and base the rest of the plant uses
A mineral-rich brine for recovery, towards near-zero liquid discharge
By-products such as lime sludge can go to local farms as agricultural lime
items.application: Conventional pre-treatment prepares the effluent. Danu Water removes the dissolved salts and turns the recovered salt into reagents, producing reclaimed cooling water and recovered minerals.

items.name: Cooling water for data centres
items.tagline: Computing without the drinking water.
items.card: Unlocks harder aquifer and well water for data centre cooling, and raises cycles of concentration.
items.problem: Data centre cooling towers are often restricted to soft fresh water and low cycles of concentration by water-quality limits, so they draw heavily on mains supply and blow down large volumes.
benefits: Harder aquifer, well and borehole sources become usable
Substantially higher cycles of concentration and less blowdown
Blowdown can be treated and recirculated
Lower antiscalant use
items.application: Conditions make-up water and treats blowdown for recirculation. Silica pre-treatment is advised at some sites.

name: Hard water & groundwater
card: Soften hard water without salt or sludge, and make well, aquifer and brackish water usable.
title: Hard water, wells and brackish sources
lede: Many businesses and communities rely on boreholes, aquifers and rivers whose water is hard, or getting saltier. Danu Water removes hardness and salts to the level each use needs, without regenerant chemicals or a large waste stream.

items.name: Brackish and well water
items.tagline: When your source is getting saltier.
items.card: Makes brackish wells and aquifers usable, with high recovery and less to dispose of.
items.problem: Over-abstraction, drought and seawater intrusion are making wells and aquifers saltier. Reverse osmosis struggles with solids, scaling and low recovery, leaving a large concentrate to manage.
benefits: High water recovery from every cubic metre pumped
Copes with scaling-prone and variable water
A smaller concentrate that can be used rather than dumped
items.application: Treats brackish or saline well water to the quality needed for irrigation, process or supply, adjusting as the source changes.

name: Desalination
card: Push past reverse osmosis' ceiling: more water from every plant and far less brine, without extra heat or chemicals.
title: Push desalination past reverse osmosis' ceiling
lede: Reverse osmosis does the bulk of the work cheaply, until scaling limits recovery. Past that point, the usual options mean more chemicals, more heat or more footprint. Danu Water takes over at exactly that point, recovering more water and shrinking the brine that is so costly to dispose of.

items.name: Brine reduction for brackish RO
items.tagline: More water, much less brine.
items.card: Treats RO concentrate to lift overall recovery from about 75% to 95%, cutting brine volume by around 80%.
items.problem: Brackish RO is usually limited to 70–85% recovery by scaling in the concentrate. For inland plants, getting rid of the remaining brine, by thermal treatment, evaporation ponds or deep wells, can be the largest cost of the whole plant.
benefits: Overall recovery raised to around 95%
Brine volume cut by about 80%, so disposal energy and costs fall dramatically
A smaller, more concentrated brine for thermal treatment or salt recovery
Strongest when designed into new plants, and still worthwhile as a retrofit
items.application: Sits on the RO concentrate, recovering water to potable-range quality and leaving a much smaller brine. Selective separation can also recover specific salts for reuse instead of discharging them.

items.name: Finishing for seawater and industrial sites
items.tagline: Finish the job without more chemicals, heat or space.
items.card: Breaks past RO's limits on recovery or purity at space-constrained sites such as LNG terminals and floating platforms.
items.problem: Adding RO capacity drives the same scaling problem harder. Thermal evaporation works but brings real energy, space and complexity costs, and both routes usually need ongoing chemical dosing.
benefits: Self-cleaning by design, with no downtime for chemical clean-in-place
No scale-control chemicals needed on demanding feedwater
Compact skids that suit space-constrained and floating sites
Fewer chemical deliveries and a smaller, cleaner reject stream for permitting
items.application: Follows RO in the water train, taking it past its ceiling to potable-grade output with a smaller, easier-to-manage reject stream.
